scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The manuscript presents a significant advancement in self-supervised learning, supported by a systematic, well-documented, and highly thorough empirical evaluation. The methodology for data curation and training optimization is sound and well-justified, and the results provide a clear, convincing case for the efficacy of the proposed models. The study maintains high standards for reporting, comparisons, and analysis of both performance and societal impact.

The recent breakthroughs in natural language processing for model pretraining on large
quantities of data have opened the way for similar foundation models in computer vision.
These models could greatly simplify the use of images in any system by producing general-
purpose visual features, i.e., features that work across image distributions and tasks without
finetuning. This work shows that existing pretraining methods, especially self-supervised
methods, can produce such features if trained on enough curated data from diverse sources.
We revisit existing approaches and combine different techniques to scale our pretraining in
terms of data and model size. Most of the technical contributions aim at accelerating and
stabilizing the training at scale. In terms of data, we propose an automatic pipeline to build

In this work, we explore if self-supervised learning has the potential to learn general-purpose visual features if
pretrained on a large quantity of curated data. We revisit existing discriminative self-supervised approaches
that learn features at both the image and patch level, such as iBOT (Zhou et al., 2022a), and we reconsider
some of their design choices under the lens of a larger dataset. Most of our technical contributions are tailored
toward stabilizing and accelerating discriminative self-supervised learning when scaling in model and data
sizes. These improvements make our approach around 2× faster and require 3× less memory than similar
discriminative self-supervised methods, allowing us to leverage longer training with larger batch sizes.

pipeline to filter and rebalance datasets from an
extensive collection of uncurated images. This pipeline is inspired by pipelines used in NLP (Wenzek et al.,
2020), where data similarities are used instead of external metadata and do not require manual annotation.
A major difficulty when dealing with images in the wild is to rebalance concepts and avoid overfitting on a

We gathered a small but diverse corpus of 142M images to validate our approach.

evidence.excerpt:
we provide a variety of pretrained visual models, called DINOv2, trained with different Vision
Transformers (ViT) (Dosovitskiy et al., 2016) architectures on our data. We release all the models and
the code to retrain DINOv2 on any data. We validate the quality of DINOv2 on various computer vision
benchmarks at both image and pixel levels as we scale them, as summarized in Fig. 2. We conclude that self-
supervised pretraining alone is a good candidate for learning transferable frozen features that are competitive
with the best openly available weakly-supervised models.

We consider several improvements to train models at a larger scale. We train models on A100 GPUs using
PyTorch 2.0. The code and pretrained models are made available under Apache 2.0 license1. The details of
our models are in the appendix, Table 17. With the same hardware, compared to the iBOT implementation,
the DINOv2 code runs around2× faster using only1/3 of the memory.
Fast and memory-efficient attention.We implemented our own version of FlashAttention (Dao et al.,
2022) to improve memory usage and speed on the self-attention layers. Our version is on par with or
better than the original on all cases considered, while covering more use-cases and hardware. Due to the
GPU hardware specifics, the efficiency is best when the embedding dimension per head is a multiple of
64, and the matrix operations are even better when the full embedding dimension is a multiple of 256.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The reported gains are corroborated across many established third-party benchmarks that were not used as optimization signals for the final models.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established on external benchmarks including ImageNet variants, iNaturalist, ADE20k, Cityscapes, NYUd, KITTI, Oxford/Paris retrieval, and video datasets using frozen features with linear probes or standard decoders.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The models are trained with DINO and iBOT losses, Sinkhorn-Knopp centering, KoLeo regularization, and other recipe components, with ablations optimized against ImageNet-1k k-NN and linear-probe performance.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The claims regarding improved scalability, training efficiency, and feature performance (e.g., surpassing previous SSL methods and competing with weakly-supervised ones) are strongly supported by the experimental results across diverse benchmarks. The ablation studies (e.g., regarding the curation pipeline and loss components) clearly demonstrate the contribution of the individual design choices.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The paper performs a robust and extensive evaluation covering image classification (ImageNet-1k, robustness benchmarks), instance recognition, semantic segmentation, and depth estimation. The comparisons include both self-supervised and weakly-supervised models (e.g., OpenCLIP), and the authors utilize appropriate evaluation protocols, including linear probing and zero-shot transfer, to demonstrate the utility of their frozen features.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The models are evaluated against diverse, widely-used, and established external benchmarks that were not involved in the training or selection of the models.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Performance is established through an extensive suite of standard, established third-party benchmarks (ImageNet, ADE20k, KITTI, NYUd, etc.) utilizing frozen features evaluated via linear probes or standard task-specific decoders.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The DINOv2 models were trained using a combination of DINO and iBOT objectives with centering, KoLeo regularization, and other stability techniques to maximize objective-specific performance during pretraining.

primary.limitations: The authors appropriately note the environmental cost of training these large-scale models, although the estimate primarily covers electricity consumption of the GPUs. They also acknowledge and analyze limitations regarding potential biases, noting their models still exhibit biases toward Western/high-income data sources, providing a balanced transparency regarding the broader impact of their work.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is rigorous, combining architectural improvements (e.g., FlashAttention, FSDP), training stability refinements (KoLeo regularizer, untying heads), and a systematic data curation pipeline (deduplication and similarity-based retrieval). The study effectively addresses the challenges of scaling self-supervised learning, and the implementation details are sufficiently provided to support reproducibility.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a significant advancement in self-supervised learning, supported by a systematic, well-documented, and highly thorough empirical evaluation. The methodology for data curation and training optimization is sound and well-justified, and the results provide a clear, convincing case for the efficacy of the proposed models. The study maintains high standards for reporting, comparisons, and analysis of both performance and societal impact.
primary.scoped_contribution: This study introduces DINOv2, a series of self-supervised vision transformers pretrained on a large, curated dataset (LVD-142M). The paper provides a comprehensive methodology for stable scaling of discriminative self-supervised learning, resulting in frozen visual features that demonstrate competitive or superior performance across a wide array of downstream vision tasks.
